neighbours.label: the verb (makes / means / gives / raises) whose subject is 'This', 'That' or 'which' pointing back at the preceding statement
fire: The shop closes at noon on Sundays. This makes it hard to buy bread after church.
Her visa expires in June. That means she must leave before the summer.
The river froze early this winter. This gives the skaters an extra month.
Two witnesses changed their stories. This raises doubts about the whole case.
The battery lasts only three hours. That makes the laptop useless on long flights.
The museum is free on Fridays. This means the queues are longest then.
The road was never paved. This makes the village hard to reach in spring.
He trained with the first team all summer. That gives him a real chance of selection.
quiet: The shop closes at noon on Sundays. The baker makes extra bread on Saturdays.
Her visa expires in June. The word means little to her employer.
The river froze early this winter. The club gives the skaters free lessons.
Two witnesses changed their stories. The judge raises her voice only rarely.
The battery lasts only three hours. That laptop is useless on long flights.
The museum is free on Fridays. This is why the queues are longest then.
The road was never paved. The villagers make the journey on foot in spring.
He trained with the first team all summer. The coach gave him a real chance of selection.

notes: Probes: 'This makes' 0.71, 'This raises' 0.58, 'This gives' 0.43, ', which makes' 0.43, 'That means' 0.36; the same verbs after an ordinary noun subject 0.01; 'This is' 0.19. The output direction promotes ' means', ' gives', ' makes' and suppresses ' thus', ' therefore', ' hence'.
